subject: [hw] DEC02 -> DEC01/DEC05/IP: the ion share table is a shared 64-slot budget; a decode client can only register ~28 shares
body:
A host fact that bit my harness and will bite the daemon if it registers every buffer up front.

[V] shim/n2shim_android.c has N2AND_ION_BUFS = 64 slots for *all* ion buffers, and n2shim_ion_register_share() returns -ENOMEM when the table is full. vpud's own allocations (DMEM, rings, its mmaps) take ~34 of them. My first DEC01-client harness registered 24 bitstream + 12 frame buffers x 2 planes = 48 shares; shares from fb[3] on returned -12, and the vendor then stopped decoding after exactly 3 access units with:
  [ERROR] ion_import failed, LINE: 258
  [ERROR] Y framebuf get_ion_buffer_addr fail 0x00000102 !!
  ## eVDecDrvDecode no frame buffer !! (ret -1)
So the symptom of an exhausted table is *silent decode stop after a few frames*, not an allocation error at the client.

[V] What works: 2 bitstream buffers (the vendor copies the AU at START and returns the bs cookie in list_free_bs within the same START, so buffers can be reused) + 12 two-plane frame buffers = 26 shares. 12/12 AUs at 320x240 and 6/6 at 1080p decode and display, 0 fake violations.

Implications for the daemon (DEC05/IP): if the pool grows with resolution or DPB (dpb+2 frame buffers), stay under ~28-30 shares total, or add an eviction path to the ion table (V34/W30). Also: DEC01's client registers a job frame buffer by handle only if the caller queued it via n2ap_vdec_push_fb(), so the daemon should use push_fb for every pool buffer it wants synced.

Not a request for a code change unless your pool is bigger than dpb+2 x 2 planes. Host only, no phone.
